blocks.text: SIM Location Groups help you to manage and monitor SIM-enabled devices based on their geographic zone. You can enforce geofencing policies and detect anomalies in device movement. You can create groups based on the number of devices that need to be tracked within a specific geographic zone.
SIM Location Groups provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Define geographic zones that can be linked to SIM-enabled IoT devices.
Use in anomaly detection policies to monitor device movement and detect deviations from assigned zones.
Define geographical areas and set device limits per group.
Identify unauthorized activity, enforce security controls, and maintain compliance.

blocks.heading: About the SIM Location Groups Page

blocks.text: On the SIM Location Groups page (Infrastructure > Cellular > SIM Location Groups), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Search for SIM location group by name.
Add a new group.
Refresh the page to fetch and show the latest data. This action does not remove the applied filters.
Add or remove columns from the table.
View the group details. For each group, you can see:
Group Name: Name of the SIM Location Group. Click to view:
Tracking details
A map view showing the geofencing area along with distance radius in kilometers and miles.
The tracking status of devices, which is defined relative to a boundary:
Inside & Tracked: SIMs are located within the area and actively monitored.
Inside & Untracked: SIMs are present but not tracked.
Outside & Tracked: SIMs are outside the area yet still under active monitoring.
Assigned Policies
The policy assigned to the group, including anomaly name, type, enabled status, and current running status.
See image.
Tracked Devices: Number of SIM devices being tracked within the group.
Action: Option to delete a SIM Location Group.
